newsitem.title: UK: Britain's Labour to keep inflation goal - report.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Labour to keep inflation goal - report.

text.p: Britain's opposition Labour Party would retain an inflation target of 2.5 percent or less and establish a Bank of England (BOE) monetary policy committee as a step towards giving the central bank control of interest rate policy, the Financial Times reported on Monday.

"In the end we rejected the idea that our credibility would have been enhanced by setting the goal lower than 2.5 percent," the newspaper quoted a colleague of Labour finance spokesman Gordon Brown as saying.
No Labour official was immediately available for comment on the report.
The Financial Times said the target had been agreed with Labour leader Tony Blair and would be announced in a speech by Brown next month, after he had held talks with BOE governor Eddie George.

"Brown is also expected to give more detail on the steps Labour would take to give the Bank autonomous control of the setting of interest rates, subject to the pre-determined inflation target," the newspaper said.
Labour, which has been in opposition since 1979, has been traditionally viewed in financial circles as being more of a high-inflation party than the ruling Conservatives.
Britain is due to hold a general election by May 22 but it could be called earlier.
